name: Enterprise Strategy & AI Orchestrator
tag: Build automation pipelines visually, with governance controls and strategy calculators built in.

scenarios.title: Build a governed pipeline
scenarios.ask: Build a contract intake pipeline for {contracts} contracts a month with {gates} approval gates.

inputs.label: Minutes of manual work per contract

steps: Laid out 6 steps: receive, extract terms, risk score, route, approve, file.
Added {gates} approval gates and a log of every model decision.
Flags about {=round(contracts * 0.12)} contracts a month with unusual terms for legal.
Ran last month's contracts through the pipeline as a dry run.
followups: Only roles you allow. Every change is versioned and needs sign-off before going live.
Can auditors see why a contract was flagged?
Yes. Each decision shows the inputs, the rule or model used and who approved it.

scenarios.title: Compare automation options
scenarios.ask: We're choosing between automating {processes} processes. Rank them by value and effort.
steps: Scored each process by hours saved, error cost and build effort.
Top {=max(2, round(processes / 3))} processes give most of the value.
Grouped them into two waves by shared systems.
Noted which ones touch personal data and need extra review.
followups: Hours saved times your hourly cost, plus fewer errors, minus build and run costs. All inputs are visible and editable.
It's an estimate to rank options. Real numbers come from the first wave's results.

scenarios.title: Governance check on existing automations
scenarios.ask: We already run {bots} automations built by different teams. Check them against our policies.
steps: Listed {bots} automations, owners and what data each touches.
{=max(1, round(bots * 0.2))} have no named owner. {=max(1, round(bots * 0.1))} send data outside approved systems.
Drafted fixes and owner requests for each.
followups: Not on its own. It recommends a pause for high-risk ones and the owner or admin decides.
Monthly is common. The orchestrator can run the check on a schedule.
